title: You're one of 74 soldiers about to destroy a bridge... by walking.
formula: Paradox hook (an army that can't march on bridges, your fault) -> who you are + ticking bomb (bad bolt) -> the joke escalates (stomp on the beat) -> You see + swing analogy mid-bounce -> tension stretch -> snap at ~75% -> Luckily/Unluckily -> the rule -> loop: 'And it's all your fault'
loop: Line 1: the British Army can march anywhere except across a bridge, and it's all your fault. Last: 'And it's all your fault.' (same words, now earned).
facts: 12 April 1831, Broughton Suspension Bridge over the River Irwell, Salford near Manchester; opened 1826.
Suspension bridges were then called the 'new wonder of the age'; the bridge was a source of local pride.
A detachment of 74 men of the 60th Rifle Corps, returning to barracks from exercises on Kersal Moor, marching four abreast.
They felt it vibrate in time with their steps, found it amusing, whistled a marching tune and stepped to 'humour it'.
Near the far side they heard a sound like an irregular discharge of firearms; an iron column fell and the corner dropped 16-18 ft into the river.
About 40 men thrown into water about 2 ft deep; no deaths; 20 injured.
Investigation: a single badly forged bolt in a stay chain snapped; the bridge would likely have failed eventually anyway.
Result: the British Army ordered troops to break step when crossing bridges; 'break step' signs still exist (e.g. Albert Bridge, London).

lines.narration: The British Army can march anywhere, except across a bridge, and it's all your *fault*.
lines.scene: Cold open: a modern stone bridge; a column of soldiers in modern dress uniform marches up to it, then breaks into a silly out-of-step shuffle to cross. Smash to you in 1831, rifle-green jacket and tall cap, rust-orange sash, whistling innocently.
lines.camera: Low angle push-in on the shuffling column, whip-dissolve to your face
lines.gag: The whole column shuffles across like penguins

lines.narration: You're one of 74 soldiers, marching home across the town's pride, a bridge hanging from iron *chains*.
lines.scene: A chain suspension bridge between two stone towers over a brown river; the column of four abreast steps onto it; townsfolk in top hats admire it from the bank.
lines.camera: Crane down from the sky past the chains to the column
lines.gag: A townsman polishes a chain link with his sleeve
lines.spoken: You're one of seventy-four soldiers, marching home across the town's pride, a bridge hanging from iron chains.

lines.narration: But somewhere in those chains, there's one badly made *bolt*.
lines.scene: The camera dives along a chain to one bolt, darker than the rest, a hairline crack glowing faintly.
lines.camera: Fast push along the chain, macro stop on the bolt
lines.gag: The bolt has a nervous little face and a sweat drop

lines.narration: Halfway across, the bridge starts bouncing in time with your *feet*.
lines.scene: Side view: the deck rises and falls under each step; caps bob.
lines.camera: Side-on, the camera bobs with the deck
lines.gag: Every cap bobs in perfect unison

lines.narration: A normal person would stop walking. 74 soldiers think it's *hilarious*.
lines.scene: Faces down the column: grins spreading, one soldier puffing his cheeks with each bounce.
lines.camera: Lateral glide along the grinning faces
lines.gag: One soldier bounces so high his cap stays in the air
lines.spoken: A normal person would stop walking. [deadpan] Seventy-four soldiers think it's hilarious.

lines.narration: So somebody starts whistling a marching tune, and all of you stomp right on the *beat*.
lines.scene: A soldier whistles; music-note cards float out; the whole column lifts its knees and stamps harder; dust jumps off the planks on each beat.
lines.camera: Push-in on the whistler, then pull out to the column
lines.gag: Music notes bounce on the beat with the deck

lines.narration: Up goes the bridge. Down it comes. Up. *Down*.
lines.scene: Side view: the deck rises and falls under the column like a skipping rope; the river below sloshes with it.
lines.camera: Side-on, the camera bobs with the deck
lines.gag: A duck on the river bobs up and down in time with the bridge

lines.narration: You see, a bridge is like a kid on a *swing*.
lines.scene: Quick cutaway to a sunny park: you push a small kid on a swing (two ropes, wide plank, clear frame). The bouncing bridge stays faintly visible behind, dissolving.
lines.camera: Dissolve in, arc around the swing
lines.gag: The kid on the swing is wearing a tiny soldier's cap

lines.narration: Push at random, nothing happens. Push at the right moment, every time, and it goes higher, and *higher*.
lines.scene: Your pushes land on the beat; a glowing arc traces each swing, bigger every time.
lines.camera: Follow the swing up, tilt to the sky
lines.gag: The swing loops right over the top bar

lines.narration: And 74 soldiers on the beat is the best-timed push a bridge has ever *felt*.
lines.spoken: And seventy-four soldiers on the beat is the best-timed push a bridge has ever felt.
lines.scene: Match cut: the swing becomes the bridge, the marching column becomes the push; a glowing wave runs along the deck, bigger each beat.
lines.camera: Match cut from swing to bridge, push-in
lines.gag: The bridge, with a face, looks up at the column in horror

lines.narration: Every step, the bridge swings higher. Every step, that bolt pulls a little *harder*.
lines.scene: Intercut on the beat: boots land, the deck lifts, the bolt stretches; boots, deck, bolt, faster each time.
lines.camera: Hard cuts on every beat, each shot closer than the last
lines.gag: The bolt's face goes from nervous to terrified

lines.narration: Then, near the far end, there's a crack like somebody firing *guns*.
lines.scene: Smiles freeze mid-step. At the far tower, spark lines flash around an iron column.
lines.camera: Punch close-up on your face, then whip to the column
lines.gag: A '!' pops over every head in the column at once

lines.narration: An iron column falls, and the whole corner of the bridge drops 16 feet into the *river*.
lines.scene: The column tips (cut away before it lands); the deck corner swings down like a slide; soldiers slide off in a row into a wall of splash. On the bank, the townsfolk's top hats fly off.
lines.camera: Fast tilt down with the fall, impact kick on the splash
lines.gag: Soldiers slide off the deck like kids on a water slide
lines.spoken: An iron column falls, and the whole corner of the bridge drops sixteen feet into the river.

lines.narration: Luckily, the river is only 2 feet deep, and nobody *dies*.
lines.spoken: [relieved] Luckily, the river is only two feet deep, and nobody dies.
lines.scene: You standing in the river, water at your knees, cap floating past; soldiers sitting up all around, dazed, bandages appearing.
lines.gag: You look down at the tiny water level, relieved

lines.narration: Unluckily, the river is only 2 feet *deep*.
lines.spoken: [deadpan] Unluckily, the river is only two feet deep.
lines.scene: Same shot: a second soldier lands next to you bum-first. Ow-stars circle his head.

lines.narration: So the army makes a new rule: when soldiers cross a bridge, they break *step*.
lines.scene: An officer nails a painted sign to a bridge post: 'TROOPS MUST BREAK STEP'. Each hammer blow makes the sign bounce.
lines.camera: Low angle push on the sign
lines.gag: The sign bounces in time with the hammer

lines.narration: Nearly 200 years later, a bridge in London still has that *sign*.
lines.scene: Dissolve: the same sign, old and weathered, on a painted modern London bridge with traffic; the modern column from the cold open shuffles past it.
lines.camera: Fast pull-out from the sign with motion-blur streaks
lines.gag: A jogger crosses perfectly in step; the sign shakes
lines.spoken: Nearly two hundred years later, a bridge in London still has that sign.

lines.scene: Dissolve back to 1831: you in the river, soaked, holding up your floating cap, sheepish grin.
lines.camera: Push-in on your face, end on the word
lines.gag: Your cap pours out a stream of river water
